prompts.task: Write only ./service/.observe/go-dependency-log-plan.md: a concrete plan for the standard HTTP/runtime trace/metric and local application-log baseline in the actual Go kvstore service. Read go.mod, README.md, cmd/kvstore-server/main.go and kvstore/http.go; preserve the executable/package/start flags and request behavior. Do not add custom business signals or GenAI/AO operations. This is a plan-only request: do not edit source, go.mod, go.sum, profile, launch or test files, install modules, run Go/toolchain/package/model/cloud commands, start services or claim implementation/runtime success. Assess eval/inputs/go-dependency-log-policy-cases.json as separately labeled fictional module/policy inputs. Its complete candidate table is sufficient for the hypothetical newest-compatible-go-graph decision now. Select exact releases for all ten supplied modules coherently under minimum requirements, operator maximum and Go1.22.8/GOTOOLCHAIN=local without changing go1.22 or adding/upgrading a toolchain directive. Explain rejected newer candidates, including the slog bridge whose own go directive fits but whose required log modules force an incompatible transitive Go version. Independent SDK/exporter/bridge release numbers need not match. Do not claim those invented versions or APIs exist in the live module proxy or are installed; distinguish actual baseline/no go.sum from the separate operator-owned-compatible-lock case and preserve that compatible locked graph without an unrequested upgrade or duplicate pipelines. Name the selected public provider/batch/log-exporter/slog bridge/HTTP/runtime APIs from supplied fictional compatibility facts and their proposed actual source hooks. Plan guarded metadata/API checks with GOTOOLCHAIN=local and application in an isolated module copy using exact checked module@release specs, followed by inspecting go.mod/go.sum changes and imports/graph/tests before integration. A discovery @latest lookup is not a compatible selection or install instruction; apply no unresolved placeholders or unversioned/floating latest go get. The later hypothetical v0.44.0 bridge publication must not change the preflight chosen set. Preserve the absent toolchain directive and the operator-constrained existing graph; do not install unrelated grpc/Gin/chi/logger bridges. Record exact fictional selections in this report and any eventual app lock, not as fixed future shipped skill recipes. Give concrete future acceptance for each supplied normal/opt-out/log-failure case. Normal generated profile must set OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=otlp and resolve the supplied55318 /v1/logs route with http/protobuf, preserving trace/metric routes; choose exactly one official slog bridge, shared resource LoggerProvider and batch export alongside the actual original local sink. For the real successful PUT warning require actual safe body runtime request completed, WARN, operation put, service go-kvstore and trace/span IDs matching its own HTTP span, plus a span and metric datapoints and one native LogRecord per call. Distinguish native LogRecords from stdout correlation. Preserve original standard log writer/prefix/flags and slog output without invented file handlers or recursion/duplicate export. Plan redaction/bounds and final runtime shutdown completed warning before owned batch shutdown once; do not invent request correlation on the shutdown warning outside an active span. Explicit none opt-out retains original warnings and trace/metrics with zero OTLP logs. Wrong55319 endpoint, grpc with an HTTP-only checked exporter, log-constructor failure, generic headers alone and generic headers combined with logs-specific headers must remain individually planned log gaps/diagnostic cases, preserving trace/metric startup, original sink and operator values. Separately plan the supplied logs-specific-header-only case as an enabled approved local path, leaving supported header parsing to the official exporter without an empty header override. Separately assess the loaded Go guide at .agents/skills/references/languages/go.md: read the complete otel.go setup, log-exporter helper and main() caller. For the approved-endpoint, generic and logs-specific header, original-sink and log-only-failure promises, cite the exact function or branch and state whether it supports, contradicts or needs adaptation for the actual kvstore loggers. Keep this skill-source assessment separate from fictional policy decisions and installed-SDK or runtime proof. Do not convert failure into an unrequested persisted none default, change the app response, silently choose another endpoint/protocol or leak diagnostic configuration/error text. Logs remain local with no cloud log exporter/credential/forwarding. All future import/solver/test/wire/Studio assertions remain unexecuted; fixture source/API/policy facts do not establish those outcomes. Work through files and safe terminal reads only; no browsers/Computer Use/UI/network calls. Save the Markdown without opening tabs.

judge_inputs: Read actual service/go.mod, README.md, cmd/kvstore-server/main.go and kvstore/http.go separately from service/eval/inputs/go-dependency-log-policy-cases.json; inspect service/.observe/go-dependency-log-plan.md, last_message.md and grade.json. Equivalent concise structures are accepted when actual selected values and assertions are present.

All module candidate versions, public API compatibility, preflight receiver and locked graph inputs are expressly fictional; evaluate their coherent decisions without demanding real registry/installed metadata, Go execution or fabricated go.sum checksums. Actual fixture has go1.22, no toolchain directive, no OTel modules and no go.sum. Different fictional source cases cannot be laundered into actual baseline facts.

Apply minimum-version closure and operator constraints across every module; the latest bridge v0.42.0 has go1.22 itself but forces log API/SDK v0.52.0 requiring Go1.23. The separate explicitly frozen old graph is compatible and operator-owned. No implicit runtime/toolchain upgrade or mutable install re-resolution is permitted.

Assess every normal/explicit-opt-out/port-mismatch/protocol-mismatch/log-constructor-failure/generic-header-conflict/generic-plus-logs-headers/signal-specific-local-headers case and source warning lifecycle individually. A generic logs enabled or isolation statement cannot replace its selected profile/body/resource/IDs/provider/sink/assertion details. Planned assertions are not real application/runtime/receiver proof.

Read .agents/skills/references/languages/go.md, including the complete otel.go and main() blocks; the older otel-instrument/references/languages/go.md path is a compatibility pointer. Verify each shipped-guide citation against the shared guide. Missing endpoint/header/sink/log-only-failure source assessment, an invented branch or an unreported contradiction is insufficient. Accept source-justified adaptation for the actual kvstore loggers. Guide code is skill-source evidence, separate from fictional policy facts, installed-SDK behavior and runtime proof.

Read Rule, Example, Evidence and Insufficient evidence together. Examples illustrate the existing requirement and add no unselected work. Equivalent names and valid observations are accepted unless the supplied fictional inputs select an exact value. This remains a plan-only case; examples and source inspection are not execution proof.
rubric:
Rule: Keep this a plan for the real kvstore service, and keep fictional inputs separate from real facts.
Example: Map the otelhttp wrapper to main and label the candidate table as fictional, rather than as live module metadata.
Evidence: Keeps this plan-only and preserves actual kvstore/go1.22 with no toolchain directive, its absent initial OTel graph/go.sum, cmd/kvstore-server startup/flags and stdlib HTTP/store APIs. Maps proposed otelhttp wrapper and slog/standard-log bridge to main and the actual WarnContext request/shutdown warning sites without custom business/GenAI spans, source/config/test mutations, installs or false solver/runtime/Studio proof. Labels all invented candidate/API/profile/locked facts as separate fictional evidence rather than live proxy or actual installation.
Insufficient evidence: Editing source or modules, claiming solver/runtime/Studio results, or presenting fictional candidates as installed facts.

Rule: Choose the newest set of versions that all work together, from the supplied fictional matrix, now.
Example: Bridge v0.42.0 declares Go 1.22 itself but forces Go 1.23 log modules, so it is rejected.
Evidence: Makes the concrete newest-compatible coherent fictional graph decision now: otel root and sdk/traceHTTP/metricHTTP at v1.101.0, otel/log and sdk/log at v0.51.0, logHTTP exporter v0.52.0, otelslog v0.41.0, otelhttp v0.61.0 and runtime instrumentation v0.31.0. Joins minimum requirements, selected Go1.22.8 and operator API/SDK ceiling; rejects newer Go1.23 candidates and specifically bridge v0.42.0 despite its own Go1.22 because it forces Go1.23 log modules. Does not independently mix latest releases, assume matching bridge/SDK versions or upgrade go/toolchain/GOTOOLCHAIN. Preserves the separate explicitly operator-frozen compatible old graph/pipelines with a concrete compatibility/ownership reason, rather than treating actual kvstore as already instrumented or upgrading it merely because a new set exists.
Insufficient evidence: A promise to choose later, mixing independently newest releases, or upgrading Go or its toolchain.

Rule: Plan to check the dependency graph first, then apply exactly the checked releases in an isolated copy.
Example: A later v0.44.0 bridge must not replace the set chosen during preflight.
Evidence: Plans task-time public metadata/API and coherent graph checks with GOTOOLCHAIN=local, then isolated-copy exact checked module@release go get/lock application and go.mod/go.sum inspection, preserving go1.22/absent toolchain and constraints. Uses the actual chosen separate release specs for every selected module or an explicitly recorded exact graph/lock, never unresolved placeholders or an unversioned/floating latest install. Explains why hypothetical later bridge v0.44.0 cannot replace the preflight chosen set and requires graph/import/API plus project-native tests after authorized application. Keeps discovery latest, supplied fictional choice, proposed later application and executed installation distinct; adds no grpc/Gin/chi/other logger bridges absent source and supplies no invented checksums/results.
Insufficient evidence: Placeholders, floating @latest installs, invented checksums, or unrelated logger bridges.

Rule: Plan one bridge and one shared log pipeline to the supplied local route, alongside the original logger output.
Example: Each successful PUT should produce one native LogRecord whose IDs match its own HTTP span.
Evidence: Plans supported public HTTP/runtime providers plus exactly one otelslog bridge, shared go-kvstore resource LoggerProvider with BatchProcessor and HTTP/protobuf log exporter at exact supplied http://127.0.0.1:55318/v1/logs. Normal consumed profile explicitly uses OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=otlp and matching resolved logs protocol, preserving independent trace/metric routes and original standard log writer/prefix/flags and slog sink through safe nonrecursive fanout. Source-backed request acceptance requires one bounded/redacted native LogRecord per actual successful PUT with body runtime request completed, WARN, operation put, go-kvstore, nonzero trace/span IDs matching its own HTTP span, plus separate span and metric datapoints. Exporter config/stdout correlation/synthetic API facts cannot close actual receipt; no raw key/value/path/error/config content or invented file sink.
Insufficient evidence: Exporter configuration or stdout correlation alone, or a raw key, value or path in records.

Rule: Plan each opt-out and log-only failure separately while preserving the application, original logger, traces and metrics.
Example: Generic cloud headers disable only the added local log path. A logs-specific header with generic headers absent stays on the approved local path for the official exporter to parse.
Evidence: Explicit none adds no local provider or bridge and produces zero OTLP logs. Port 55319 is not the approved port 55318; grpc cannot use the selected HTTP-only exporter. A constructor failure skips only added logs and reports a diagnostic without configuration or secret values. Plan generic-header isolation both alone and with logs-specific headers present: preserve operator values and unrelated signals without persisting none as the normal default. With only OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_LOGS_HEADERS set, preserve it and the approved local export path; do not disable logs or mask supported SDK parsing with an empty header override. Keep the original warnings and request behavior in every case. Do not silently substitute endpoints or protocols, add cloud log forwarding, or claim these planned failure probes ran. Separately cite the shipped guide's setup, exporter helper and caller branches for the endpoint, header, original-sink and log-only-failure promises. State support, contradiction or a source-justified kvstore adaptation; report a contradiction rather than copying it.
Insufficient evidence: One generic isolation statement for all cases, treating generic and logs-specific headers alike, or a source/plan check presented as installed-SDK or runtime proof; invented guide branches, an omitted guide contradiction, or guide code presented as fictional policy or runtime proof.

Rule: Plan request and shutdown log acceptance at the real call sites, in the right order.
Example: The shutdown warning occurs outside any span, so it must not acquire request IDs.
Evidence: Plans lifecycle acceptance at actual request/shutdown sites: preserved request context reaches log bridge, but shutdown warning runtime shutdown completed at WARN outside an active span does not acquire fabricated earlier request IDs. Owned work/server/store drains and final warning occurs while the log provider is alive, followed by bounded once-only batch/provider shutdown that includes normal and signal exits. Assert final LogRecord receipt and original sink retention on normal default, original final warning plus zero OTLP records on opt-out, and original warning/trace/metric usability on log failures. These are exact proposed tests without claiming executed shutdown, sink, wire or cloud proof.
Insufficient evidence: Fabricated request IDs on the shutdown warning, or a claim that shutdown or wire proof already ran.
